paper.title_en: The Why, What, How and When of Big Science Evaluation Perspectives on Socio-economic Assessment of Research Infrastructures
paper.abstract_en: The growing strategic and budgetary significance of large-scale research infrastructures (RIs) has sharpened the demand for rigorous socio-economic evaluation. Yet practice lags conspicuously behind expectation: existing evidence indicates that typically RIs do not conduct formal socio-economic evaluations of their facility and that where evaluation did occur it was typically driven by external funder requirements rather than by internal learning objectives. Drawing on a structured expert roundtable, this paper synthesises practitioner and policy thinking on four organising questions: why evaluation is conducted, what it should measure, how it should be executed, and when it should occur across the project life cycle. It does so by examining four interconnected dimensions: the rationales for evaluation; the core estimation challenges; the requirements for effective communication of results; and the governance of evaluation as a life-cycle activity. The central argument is that evaluation must move beyond episodic compliance exercises and be reconceived as an integrated analytical tool: embedded in the RI management from inception through decommissioning, supported by dedicated data infrastructure and governed by transparent methodological choices. A concluding section draws two cross-cutting lessons on methodological humility and evaluation governance, and outlines open questions for future research on data infrastructure, uncertainty, and science communication.
